The Court Made The Following:
 Order

1. Petitioners, who are arrayed as accused nos.2 to 6 in Crime No.97/2023 registered by Mysuru City Women Police Station, Mysuru, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323 and 149 of IPC, are before this Court with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings in the aforesaid case pending on the file of the VII Additional Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.) and JMFC, Mysuru, as against them.

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

3. FIR in Crime No.97/2023 was registered by Mysuru City Women Police Station, Mysuru, against Venugopal.B and the petitioners herein for the aforesaid offences on the complaint of respondent no.2 herein, who is the wife of accused no.1- Venugopal.

entities.text: Mysuru City Women Police Station, Mysuru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accused nos.2 and 3 are the parents of accused no.1, accused no.4 is the sister of accused no.1, accused no.5 NC: 2024:KHC:10506 is the daughter of accused no.4 and accused no.6 is allegedly the girl friend of accused no.1.
Being aggrieved by the registration of FIR in Crime No.97/2023 as against the petitioners herein, they are before this Court.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that respondent no.2/Complainant has deserted accused no.1 in the year 2018 along with her child and she is residing in her parents house ever since then.
She has been filing repeated complaints against the accused.
Accused no.1 has filed a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act before the jurisdictional Civil Court in M.C.No.8/2023 on 21.02.2023.
In the said proceedings, respondent no.2 has appeared and filed her statement of objections on 20.04.2023.
The present complaint is filed on 17.06.2023 making omnibus allegations against the relatives of accused no.1 only with an intention to harass them.

He submits that a reading of the statement of objections filed by respondent no.2 would clearly go to show that she has been residing separately ever since the year 2018 in her parents house, and therefore, he prays to allow the petition.
Per contra, the learned HCGP for respondent no.1 and learned counsel appearing for respondent no.2 have opposed the petition.
They submit that there are necessary ingredients in the complaint which would prima facie attract the alleged offences against the accused.
The allegations are made against all the accused, and therefore, there is no ground to quash the proceedings.

They submit that having regard to the averments made in the complaint, investigation is required as against all the accused, and accordingly, they pray to dismiss the petition.
6.
The material on record would go to show that the marriage of accused no.1 with respondent no.2/defacto complainant was solemnised on 05.06.2014 and from the wedlock, they have a child.

It appears that the relationship between the parties got strained, and therefore, they started residing T.K. Basavegowda vs The State Of Karnataka on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106066886/
3 separately.

sentences.text: Accused no.1, who is the husband of respondent no.2, has filed M.C.No.8/2023 before the jurisdictional Court under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act seeking a decree of restitution of conjugal rights.
The said petition was filed on 21.02.2023.
Respondent no.2 has entered appearance in the said proceedings on 20.04.2023.
In her statement of objections, she has stated that her husband had NC: 2024:KHC:10506 left her and her child in her parents house on 08.06.2018.
She has also stated that request made by her parents and other relatives with the accused persons to take her back to the matrimonial house had failed.

She has stated that with regard to an incident that had taken place on 29.10.2019, she had lodged a complaint against her husband before the Mysuru Women Police Station on 01.11.2019 and the police had summoned accused no.1 and had advised him to behave properly.

She has also stated that ever since the date her husband deserted her i.e., on 08.06.2018, he has failed to pay any maintenance to her and her child and she was completely depending on her parents for maintenance.
She has stated that her son was admitted in a School by her parents and his educational expenses was being met by them.
From a reading of the entire statement of objections filed by respondent no.2 in M.C.No.8/2023, it is evident that ever since 2018, she is residing separately.
7. The present complaint is filed on 17.06.2023 after she had filed her statement of objections in M.C.No.8/2023 before the jurisdictional Civil Court.

In the complaint, it is averred that on 07.06.2023, after the complainant received information NC: 2024:KHC:10506 that accused no.1 was likely to marry accused no.6, she and her relatives had gone to the farm house of accused no.1 and it is alleged that there was a quarrel between the two parties in the said farmhouse and the accused had assaulted the defacto complainant on the said date.

In respect of the said incident, a separate complaint was lodged before the Mysuru Women Police Station on 09.06.2023 and in the present complaint, this aspect of the matter has been admitted by the defacto complainant.

Based on the said complaint which was lodged in respect of the incident that had taken place on 07.06.2023, it appears that a case was registered and the accused named in the said complaint were summoned to the Police Station on 10.06.2023 and after recording their statements, they were sent back.

8. The allegation in the present complaint is that though the accused persons who had appeared on 10.06.2023 before the Police Station had undertaken to appear before the Police Station, thereafter,
they had failed to do so, and therefore, the complainant apprehends accused no.1 is likely to marry accused no.6 and an enquiry in the said regard is prayed in the present complaint.

Therefore, it is very clear that the present NC: 2024:KHC:10506 complaint is not lodged in respect of the incident that had taken place on 07.06.2023, wherein the defacto Complainant was allegedly assaulted.
In respect of the said incident that had taken place on 07.06.2023, a separate complaint was lodged and an enquiry was made in respect of the said complaint by the Police.

In addition to the same,
from a reading of the entire complaint averments, it is seen that no specific allegations or overt acts are made against any one of the petitioners herein.
Omnibus allegations are made in the complaint as against all the accused.

9. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Preeti Gupta and Another v. State of Jharkhand and Another reported in (2010) 7 SCC 667, has observed that implicating near relatives of the husband in a case for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC without there being specific T.K. criminal proceedings cannot be continued against any such accused.
10. It is the case of the petitioners that they are residing separately and they are not residing with accused no.1.
Merely NC: 2024:KHC:10506 for the reason that they are close relatives of accused no.1, they have been falsely implicated in the case.

Moreover, it is seen from a reading of the complaint averments that the allegations made in the present complaint do not prima facie make out a case for invoking the alleged offences against the petitioners.
So far as the incident that had taken place on 07.06.2023, a separate complaint was lodged.

Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that continuation of the present proceedings against the petitioners herein would amount to abuse of process of law and for the purpose of securing the ends of justice, it is necessary to quash the same.

11. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Criminal Petition is allowed;
(ii) The entire proceedings in Crime No.97/2023 registered by Mysuru City Women Police Station, Mysuru, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323 and 149 of IPC pending on the file of the VII Additional Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.) and JMFC,
Mysuru, as against the petitioners herein is hereby quashed;
- 10 -  NC: 2024:KHC:10506  (iii) In view of disposal of the petition,
I.A.No.1/2024 does not survive for consideration.
Sd/-
JUDGE hkh.
